messages:
sarah: Quick heads-up — noticed a canary where p95 latency is +8% vs baseline but the rollout guard didn't alert. Saw it in the heatmap slice for EU-west :thinking:
kevin: Which guard? the static threshold on `latency_p95` or the anomaly detector?
ranjit: If it's static, +8% might be under a percent-based threshold we set (we use 10% for p95). Could be a visibility vs sensitivity issue.
ida: We also have a per-tenant quota guard that silences alerts during quota throttles — any chance that fired?
sarah: No quota throttle. The curious part: the canary->baseline delta is small overall, but the user-cohort slice (mobile web) shows +20% p95.
monitoring-bot: Canary analysis finished — top deltas: mobile-web p95 +20%, api-errors +0.2pp, user-impact estimated 1.4% traffic. Link: https://console/redwood/rollouts/1965432100/analysis
kevin: That's the UI gap: canned canary view shows aggregate delta and hides high-impact slices unless you click into the heatmap. UX should elevate any slice crossing a relative-impact threshold.
ranjit: Agreed. Also, backend currently computes deltas at ingest time for overall metrics only. Per-slice deltas are expensive at query-time due to cardinality.
ida: Proposal: add a lightweight rollup job that computes per-slice 14-day rolling median and delta for slices above a traffic cutoff (e.g., >0.5% traffic). That reduces cost and surfaces only meaningful slices.
oliver: Can we avoid more storage by computing on demand but cache results for 30m? a hybrid would cut storage and still be quick for drilldowns.
kevin: API change suggestion: expose a `rollout_signals` endpoint with params `window=14d&min_traffic=0.5pct&cache_ttl=30m`. Example:

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood/rollouts/1965432100/signals?window=14d&min_traffic=0.5pct"
```

Returns top slices and delta vectors.
ranjit: That helps UX but watch out for cardinality explosion — some customers have 10k+ URL paths. Need guardrails: limit to top N slices by traffic and an admission filter on tag cardinality.
sarah: Also, alerting: we should distinguish absolute vs relative alerts. For small baseline p95 (e.g., 50ms), a +10% is tiny in absolute terms. The guard config should allow `absolute_threshold` OR `relative_threshold` and an `impact_floor`.
ida: UX idea: in the rollout page, show three states: PASS, WARN (slice-level delta above relative but below impact_floor), FAIL (slice-level delta above relative and above impact_floor). Hover shows contributing slices.
oliver: +1. And add an "auto-snooze" option in the console when a canary spikes but traffic is < min_traffic — prevents alert noise.
kevin: Implementation notes: backend needs a `compute_rollout_deltas` job, a small index for top-slices per rollout, and the new `rollout_signals` API. Frontend needs heatmap pinning and slice-prominence rules.
ranjit: I'll sketch the job — it will iterate only top-N tag combinations per metric per-region per-day and compute rolling median. Will post pseudo config.

```
job: rollout_slice_rollup
window: 14d
top_n: 200
min_traffic_pct: 0.5
cache_ttl: 30m
```

sarah: Sounds good. Can someone volunteer to prototype the API + simple frontend pinning? If not this sprint, let's backlog and add to the rollout observability epic.
ida: I can mock the UI interactions this week and send flows.
kevin: I'll take the API prototype (node) — will post PR for schema.
ranjit: I'll own the rollup job and storage estimate. Quick note: add a metric in Cost dashboard for rollup storage so product understands tradeoffs.
sarah: Thanks all. I'll update the rollout playbook to call out the new slice prominence and impact_floor fields.
deploy-bot: Reminder: staging deployment of monitoring changes scheduled 2026-04-12 03:00 UTC :rocket:
kevin: Ping me when staging is up, I'll wire the API tests.
sarah: Closing loop here — follow-ups in #eng-platform. :thumbsup:
